name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,418

clue.text: Petty scam largely formulated and staged in same way?

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter of the word before is dropped
something formulated is worked out afresh, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A small-time con, mostly cooked up and acted out the same way as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staged' looks like part of the con story, but the whole final phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is put on stage repeatedly in roles of one kind, always cast alike.

clue.text: Sample stunning device round back of depot

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes around a letter
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a Taser is an electric stun gun
final letter

explanation.surface: Police try out a stun gun behind the depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered so that someone can try something, much like a sample.

clue.text: Antidepressant for unsuccessful London mayoral election candidate

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
Zac Goldsmith, the Conservative who lost the 2016 London mayoral race

explanation.surface: A losing candidate for Mayor of London might well need some pills to cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is the brand name of fluoxetine, a widely prescribed drug for depression.

clue.text: Box holding second part for stewed food

indicators.note: something holding another keeps it inside, so a letter sits within the first word

blocks.note: a case is a box or container
S is the abbreviation
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Boxed portions set aside for a second helping of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid in the oven.

clue.text: Tiny shoot in time of growth not new

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for the word after it

blocks.note: spring is the season when plants grow
N is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A small new shoot appearing in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or twig bearing leaves or flowers, cut from a plant.

clue.text: Dim places backing half-formed notion

indicators.note: backing means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left
only half formed means only half of the following word is kept

blocks.note: to place something is to put it
a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a half-baked idea is foolish and its backers dim.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of IDEA, ID, is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim is an informal synonym for slow-witted or lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Cuba's in genuine cessation of hostilities

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the next word

blocks.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code
genuine means true

explanation.surface: Cuba is genuinely committed to a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: Countries have one- to three-letter codes shown on car plates; Cuba's is C.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement between enemies to stop fighting for a period.

clue.text: Verbal wit? It is found amid formal expert judgment

indicators.note: something found amid others is in their middle, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a pun is wordplay
taken as written
dry can mean stiff, impersonal and formal in manner

explanation.surface: Is wordplay acceptable in serious, formal expert opinion?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the first definition-like phrase; dry here means stiffly impersonal, as in a dry official report.
explanation.definitionFit: Punditry is the giving of opinions by experts, especially commentators in the media.

clue.text: Administer varied needs round BT say

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters take a new order
round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
BT is an example of an internet service provider; say signals an example

explanation.surface: A phone company is told to handle its customers' various requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom, the UK's main phone and broadband company.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense medicine or justice is to administer it, handing it out to those who need it.

clue.text: Trim staff with hospital area about to close

blocks.note: to man a post is to staff it
intensive care unit
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Cutting hospital staff and an intensive care ward that's about to shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim is a noun here, as in a haircut; the treatment trims the fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the hands, chiefly the shaping and trimming of nails.

clue.text: Poles kept in track for promoter

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: north and south are the two poles
a spoor is the track left by an animal

explanation.surface: Polish people confined to a racetrack, waiting on whoever organises the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; here they are the compass points N and S, set inside SPO-OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor promotes or backs an event, product or person, often by funding it.

clue.text: Old boy, Greek character, entering a slum for demolition

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the letter is placed within the other letters
a building up for demolition will be knocked apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An elderly Greek man moving into a run-down tenement just before it is pulled down.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boy is the British term for a former pupil of a school, the same as a graduate or former student.

clue.text: Dodge some recalled in depressed avenue

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A Dodge car recalled by its maker, found on a run-down street.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge reads like the American car brand being recalled; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or escape it by quick movement or trickery.

clue.text: Help for mountaineers with rope - and indication of course

blocks.note: climbers hire a mountain guide to lead them
a line is a rope or cord

explanation.surface: A climbing tip: take a guide and a rope, and you'll know which route to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a rule or principle that shows the direction to take on a matter.

clue.text: Pianist with dubious expression on network beginning to shock BBC journalist

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: Elton John, the singer-songwriter famed at the piano
humph is a grunt of doubt or disapproval
RY is short for railway, a rail network
opening letter

explanation.surface: A musician pulls a doubtful face on air, about to startle a BBC reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: John Humphrys was the long-serving presenter of BBC Radio 4's Today programme, known for tough interviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrys is a Welsh broadcaster and interviewer who spent decades presenting news for the British public broadcaster.

clue.text: Goads son? That's gratuitous

blocks.note: to needle someone is to provoke them
S is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A parent provokes their son, and the teasing is uncalled for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gratuitous is uncalled for and lacking good reason, so it is unnecessary.

clue.text: Tout PR i.e. dodgy source of elaborate spin

indicators.note: something dodgy is not straight, so the letters are rearranged
the source of a word is where it starts, its initial

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter

explanation.surface: Pushing public relations, which is a shady origin for elaborate spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests PR spin-doctoring, but it is a dancer's turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a full turn on one foot in ballet, a rapid spin of the body.

clue.text: Man had inside clues possibly for inventory

indicators.note: inside says the first piece goes within the other
possibly means the word could take other forms, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: a man had is he'd, the contraction of he had
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective had insider hints, perhaps, in compiling a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule can be a written list or catalogue of items, like an inventory of goods.

clue.text: Dish that is hidden by some meat and pastry

indicators.note: something hidden by other things is covered by them, so it sits between them

blocks.note: a cut is a piece of meat
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A dish where something lurks under the meat and pastry crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' wants to be food, given the meat and pastry; it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal for an attractive person, and a cutie-pie is an endearing, attractive one.

clue.text: Worry about American and European star in noted trial

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the rest

blocks.note: care is anxiety or worry
US is the standard abbreviation
E is the abbreviation
a celeb is a celebrity, a star

explanation.surface: Concern over an American and a European celebrity caught up in a famous court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French for a famous case, used in English for a notorious trial or controversy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause célèbre is a lawsuit or issue that attracts widespread public attention and debate.

clue.text: Ammo is exploding in plant

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ammunition going off in a factory, a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, fitting the explosion; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub or tree of the pea family with feathery leaves.

clue.text: Military officer, it's said, in centre

indicators.note: it's said means as spoken, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, pronounced like the word

explanation.surface: An army colonel, so they say, sits at the heart of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the inner part of a nut or seed, hence the central core of anything.

clue.text: Immediate pinpointers to crosses?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that quickly marks the location of crossroads or crucifixes
setter's reading: the crosses voters put on ballot papers, which surveys of voters leaving the booth reveal on election night

explanation.walkthrough: Crosses are votes marked with an X; these surveys indicate where they went as soon as polling stations close.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys taken of voters as they leave polling stations give the earliest forecast of an election result.

clue.text: Remove undesirable parts from fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: to cut back or trim away unwanted parts
second meaning: a dried plum

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as removing blemishes from fruit; in fact the fruit is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a tree is to cut away dead or unwanted branches; a prune is also a dried plum.

clue.text: Excellent meal with pressure gone

indicators.note: gone means taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A great dinner, now the stress has lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal word meaning very good or excellent, like great or terrific.

clue.text: Integrate measure of alcohol with energy

blocks.note: a unit is the standard British measure of alcohol intake
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Mixing a drink in with a burst of energy, like an advert for a mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate parts is to join or combine them into a single whole.

clue.text: Disconnects adverts for peacekeepers?

blocks.note: UN peacekeeping forces are sent by the United Nations
a plug is a piece of publicity for something

explanation.surface: Someone cuts off publicity for the blue-helmeted troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Adverts for the UN would be UN plugs, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who unplugs an appliance disconnects it by pulling its lead from the socket.

clue.text: Drop record

blocks.note: first meaning: to set something down, or to land an aircraft
second meaning: to write something down on paper

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a record being dropped by a label; the two words are separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to lower something onto a surface and to write a fact down.

clue.text: English Liberal with smooth side

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation
L is the abbreviation in party politics
a smooth surface is even

explanation.surface: An English Liberal politician with a polished, slick manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Side is a team: football and cricket teams field this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team has that number of players, so the number names the team itself.

clue.text: Descent in public brawl knocking out soldiers

indicators.note: knocking out removes something, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a free-for-all is a disorderly fight open to anyone
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A street fight in which troops are knocked out, sending things downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is a rapid drop, as of a skydiver before the parachute opens, or a collapse in prices.
